summary: The sole occurrence describes appointing the cousin as king: plural human agents, zero-marked cousin as patient and malko as the assigned role. b dukṯe du babaṯṯe identifies the predecessor being replaced.
ko-Infectum advances the narrative even though the edition translates it with a German past form. No new Preterit box is warranted.

The Arabic-derived nomination verb is integrated into II. It is lexical here, without an independently established light-verb idiom. No new numbered sense, example or correction is supported by this duplicate occurrence.
